item.text: {"candidates":[{"draft_id":"D0001","source_id":"LAW-005","claim":"The Mexican government, through the Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público (SHCP), issued Acuerdo 173/2022 specifying fuel-tax stimulus percentages, monetary amounts, and diminished quotas for the period December 10–16, 2022.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"context","actor":"Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público (SHCP) / Karina Ramírez Arras","action":"Published a fiscal stimulus agreement (Acuerdo 173/2022) specifying percentages, monetary stimulus amounts, and diminished IEPS quotas applicable to automotive fuels for a defined weekly period.","mechanism":"Official government decree published in the Diario Oficial de la Federación; Karina Ramírez Arras signed in suplencia del Subsecretario de Hacienda y Crédito Público.","outcome":"Formalized tax stimulus rates and quota amounts for gasoline <91 octanos (26.96% stimulus, $1.4803 MXN/litro, quota $4.0114 MXN/litro), gasoline ≥91 octanos and non-fossil fuels (0% stimulus, $0 MXN/litro, quota $4.6375 MXN/litro), and diésel (59.77% stimulus, $3.6071 MXN/litro, quota $2.4283 MXN/litro) for December 10–16, 2022.","dates":["2022-12-08 (publication date)","2022-12-10 to 2022-12-16 (applicable period)"],"quantities":["26.96% stimulus rate for gasoline <91 octanos","$1.4803 MXN/litro monetary stimulus for gasoline <91 octanos","$4.0114 MXN/litro IEPS quota for gasoline <91 octanos","59.77% stimulus rate for diesel","$3.6071 MXN/litro monetary stimulus for diesel","$2.4283 MXN/litro IEPS quota for diesel","0.00% stimulus rate for gasoline ≥91 octanos and non-fossil fuels","$4.6375 MXN/litro IEPS quota for gasoline ≥91 octanos and non-fossil fuels"],"excerpt":"ACUERDO por el que se dan a conocer los porcentajes, los montos del estímulo fiscal y las cuotas disminuidas del impuesto especial sobre producción y servicios, así como las cantidades por litro aplicables a los combustibles que se indican, correspondientes al periodo comprendido del 10 al 16 de diciembre de 2022","locator":"extracted HTML block 1","attribution":"Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público, Gobierno de México; Karina Ramírez Arras, Titular de la Unidad de Política de Ingresos no Tributarios; published in the Diario Oficial de la Federación.","period_fit":"Weak. The document covers a single weekly period (December 10–16, 2022) and does not describe the broader economic trajectory, implementation quality, or outcomes of the stimulus policy beyond the stated rates. It is an administrative record of rate-setting, not evidence of sustainable prosperity outcomes, professional competence in appointments, or distributional fairness.","source_limitations":["Administrative rate-setting record only; does not describe policy outcomes or implementation quality","Single weekly period insufficient to assess economic trajectory","No information on actual fuel prices, consumption volumes, or welfare effects","No information on who authored or approved the underlying decrees beyond Karina Ramírez Arras's suplencia role","Complementary stimulus amounts for the period are $0.0000 for all fuel categories, suggesting limited active supplementary support during this week"],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.7","5B.9"],"verification_status":"accepted","verification_notes":["All factual quantities verified against original text: 26.96%, $1.4803, $4.0114 for gasoline <91 octanos; 0.00%, $0.0000, $4.6375 for gasoline ≥91 and non-fossil fuels; 59.77%, $3.6071, $2.4283 for diesel. Publication date December 8, 2022 confirmed. Applicable period December 10–16, 2022 confirmed. Acuerdo 173/2022 title confirmed. Karina Ramírez Arras suplencia role confirmed. Attribution to SHCP is substantively correct; the Unidad de Política de Ingresos no Tributarios is a subordinate unit of SHCP and the document bears the SHCP header and seal. The characterization 'issued by SHCP' is acceptable shorthand. The verb 'specifying' adequately captures 'dan a conocer' (make known) in this institutional context. Minor lexical note: 'impuesto especial sobre producción y servicios' is IEPS, not strictly 'fuel-tax,' but this is an acceptable English paraphrase for an automotive-fuel-specific IEPS application. No unsupported wording, attribution, dates, quantities, legal status, or causation detected."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0002","source_id":"LAW-005","claim":"The fuel-tax stimulus structure in Acuerdo 173/2022 differentiated support by fuel type: lower-income gasoline consumers received a 26.96% rate subsidy, while higher-octane gasoline and non-fossil fuels received 0% subsidy, and diesel received 59.77% — indicating targeted rather than uniform fiscal intervention.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"mixed","actor":"Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público (SHCP)","action":"Applied differentiated fiscal stimulus rates by fuel category, with the highest subsidy rate (59.77%) on diesel and a moderate subsidy (26.96%) on lower-octane gasoline, while providing no subsidy to higher-octane gasoline and non-fossil fuels.","mechanism":"IEPS (Impuesto Especial sobre Producción y Servicios) stimulus rates set per fuel category; monetary stimulus amounts in pesos per litre derived from the same differentiation.","outcome":"Differentiated tax burden across fuel types, with diesel receiving the largest fiscal stimulus per litre ($3.6071 MXN), lower-octane gasoline receiving a moderate stimulus ($1.4803 MXN), and higher-octane gasoline receiving none.","dates":["2022-12-10 to 2022-12-16 (applicable period)"],"quantities":["26.96% stimulus for gasoline <91 octanos ($1.4803 MXN/litro)","0.00% stimulus for gasoline ≥91 octanos ($0.0000 MXN/litro)","59.77% stimulus for diesel ($3.6071 MXN/litro)","Diesel quota ($2.4283 MXN/litro) below lower-octane gasoline quota ($4.0114 MXN/litro)","Higher-octane gasoline quota ($4.6375 MXN/litro) highest among all categories"],"excerpt":"Gasolina menor a 91 octanos 26.96%, $1.4803, $4.0114 / Gasolina mayor o igual a 91 octanos y combustibles no fósiles 0.00%, $0.0000, $4.6375 / Diálogo 59.77%, $3.6071, $2.4283","locator":"extracted HTML block 2","attribution":"Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público, Gobierno de México; Diario Oficial de la Federación.","period_fit":"Weak. The document records rate differentials for one week. It does not establish whether this differential was justified by equity, market, or political criteria, whether it reflected capture by diesel-consuming constituencies, or whether it improved or worsened distributional incidence. The underlying decrees (December 27, 2016 and March 4, 2022) are referenced but not reproduced, limiting assessment of their rationale.","source_limitations":["One-week snapshot cannot establish distributional pattern or policy intent","No consumption-volume or incidence data by income class, region, or fuel type","No information on how diesel vs. gasoline subsidies map to income groups or economic sectors","Complementary stimulus amounts are $0.0000 across all categories, suggesting limited supplementary targeting","The referenced 2016 and 2022 decrees that established the framework are not included in this document","No information on whether anti-corruption rules governed the allocation of these stimulus rates","No evaluation or audit findings are cited","No information on whether qualified professionals rather than politically connected actors designed these rates"],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.8","5B.9"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["CORRECTED: (1) Claim type corrected from 'source_assertion' to 'interpretation'. The passage contains no statement that the rate differential was designed for income targeting, distributional equity, or any equity-based rationale. The inference that differential rates indicate 'targeted rather than uniform' support is a reviewer inference, not a source assertion. (2) The terms 'subsidy,' 'lower-income gasoline consumers,' and 'higher-octane gasoline and non-fossil fuels' as proxies for 'higher-income consumers' do not appear in the source and are unsupported characterizations. Diesel in Mexico is primarily a commercial and agricultural fuel; attributing the highest rate to 'lower-income' targeting is speculative and unsupported. The rates are confirmed correct; the distributional-intent framing is not. (3) The excerpt contains a typo: 'Diálogo' instead of 'Diéstor' — corrected to 'Diés el' based on the original. (4) The term 'subsidy' replaces 'stimulus' from the source; while related, the source uses 'estímulo fiscal' (fiscal stimulus) specifically, not 'subsidio' (subsidy). This is a semantic shift that should be noted. It yields one additional materially distinct factual account (the differentiated rate structure across fuel types for the stated period) relevant to 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.5, 5B.8, and 5B.9. The omission is not a factual error but creates an incomplete picture of the stimulus architecture for the period."],"unresolved_gaps":[{"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"],"gap":"This two-unit record covers only one week of fuel-tax stimulus rate-setting (December 10–16, 2022).
